identity.title: OPUS: Towards Efficient and Principled Data Selection in Large Language Model Pre-training in Every Iteration

problem.claim: Improve data selection for LLM pre-training as high-quality public text becomes scarce and training shifts toward better tokens.

gap.claim: Existing approaches are described as either static heuristic filters that ignore training dynamics or dynamic criteria based on raw gradients without optimizer awareness.

contributions.claim: OPUS defines dynamic data utility in the optimizer-induced update space and scores candidates by projecting effective updates onto a target direction from a stable in-distribution proxy.
The framework combines Ghost with CountSketch for efficiency and Boltzmann sampling for diversity.
The utility score is presented as potentially usable as a static filter for identifying and removing toxic documents before training.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors propose optimizer-induced projected utility selection, distinguishing utility in optimizer-shaped update space rather than raw-gradient space.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that the scalability design incurs 4.7% additional compute overhead.
The authors report strong results across corpora, quality tiers, optimizers, and model scales.
The authors report that OPUS outperforms previous data-selection methods across training stages, including from-scratch pre-training and mid-training.

narrative_sequence.summary: High-quality public text is approaching exhaustion, motivating selection of better training tokens.
Prior methods are characterized as static and dynamics-insensitive, or dynamic but optimizer-agnostic.
OPUS evaluates optimizer-shaped effective updates against a proxy-derived target direction.
Ghost with CountSketch and Boltzmann sampling address computational cost and diversity, with 4.7% reported overhead.
The authors report broad results, cross-stage comparisons, and potential toxic-document filtering use.

source_observation.claim: The abstract defines utility in the optimizer-induced update space and contrasts this with raw-gradient criteria.

lessons.interpretation: When optimization transforms parameter updates, aligning selection with the effective update geometry may make the claimed mechanism more precise.
lessons.application: Frame a data-selection objective in the representation actually used by the training update, then state the proxy direction and projection explicitly.
lessons.exception: This framing may be unsuitable when the optimizer or its state is unavailable, unstable, or too costly to model.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide quantitative quality gains, baselines, datasets, model sizes, or statistical details for the reported results.
The toxic-document result is described as potential rather than a quantified demonstrated outcome; its detection criteria and validation are unspecified.
The abstract does not clarify how the proxy target direction is constructed or how optimizer state is handled across training stages.
